reference_title: Eurocode 7: Geotechnical Design - Part 1: General Rules
chapter_title: Annex J (informative): Checklist for construction supervision and performance monitoring

sections.title: Annex J.1: General
sections.summary: Annex J is a non-exhaustive checklist of the more important items to consider when supervising construction or monitoring the performance of a completed structure; item importance varies by project. Items specific to particular geotechnical aspects or work types are covered in the standard's numbered Sections rather than repeated here.
sections.body: The list that follows in Annex J contains the more important items that should be considered when supervising construction or monitoring the performance of the completed structure. The importance of the items will vary from project to project, and the list is explicitly not exhaustive. Items that refer to specific aspects of geotechnical engineering, or to specific types of works, have been reported in the numbered Sections of this standard (e.g. Section 9 for retaining structures, Section 5 for fill/dewatering) rather than repeated in this general checklist.
key_points: Annex J checklist is NOT exhaustive; item importance varies by project
Work-type-specific or aspect-specific supervision items are covered in the standard's own numbered Sections, not repeated here
Annex J is purely a supervision/monitoring aide-memoire -- no equations or tables
sections.applicability: Framing note for how to use the Annex J checklist alongside the section-specific supervision/monitoring requirements elsewhere in the standard.

sections.title: Annex J.2: Construction supervision
sections.summary: General items to check during construction (J.2.1): ground conditions/layout verification; ground-water flow and pore pressure regime incl. dewatering effects, seepage control, erosion/piping, water chemistry, corrosion potential; excavation-wall/base movement and stability incl. effects on nearby structures/utilities, soil pressure and pore-pressure measurement; worker safety. Water-flow/pore-pressure specific items (J.2.2): dewatering system adequacy and operation (artesian pressures, well/pump condition), disturbance control, adjoining-structure settlement, sub-horizontal drain effectiveness.
sections.body: Annex J.2.1 lists general items to be checked during construction supervision: (1) verification of ground conditions and of the location and general layout of the structure; (2) ground-water flow and pore-water pressure regime, including the effects of dewatering operations on the ground-water table, the effectiveness of measures to control seepage inflow, internal erosion processes and piping, the chemical composition of the ground-water, and corrosion potential; (3) movements, yielding, and stability of excavation walls and base, temporary support systems, effects on nearby buildings and utilities, measurement of soil pressures on retaining structures, and measurement of pore-water pressure variations resulting from excavation or loading; (4) safety of workmen with due consideration of geotechnical limit states. Annex J.2.2 lists water-flow and pore-water-pressure-specific items: (1) adequacy of systems to control pore-water pressures in all aquifers where excess pressure could affect the stability of slopes or the excavation base, including artesian pressures in an aquifer beneath the excavation, disposal of water from dewatering systems, depression of the ground-water table throughout the excavation to prevent boiling/quick conditions/piping/equipment-caused disturbance, and diversion/removal of rainfall or other surface water; (2) efficient, effective dewatering-system operation throughout construction, considering encrusting well screens, silting of wells/sumps, pump wear, and pump clogging; (3) control of dewatering to avoid disturbing adjoining structures or areas, observation of piezometric levels, and effectiveness/operation/maintenance of any water recharge systems; (4) settlement of adjoining structures or areas; (5) effectiveness of sub-horizontal borehole drains.
key_points: J.2.1 general items: ground-condition/layout verification; ground-water/pore-pressure regime and dewatering effects; seepage/erosion/piping/corrosion; excavation wall/base movement and stability; effects on neighbours; worker safety

J.2.2 water-flow items: dewatering adequacy incl. artesian pressure control, boiling/piping prevention, well/pump maintenance, avoiding disturbance to adjoining structures, piezometric observation, recharge-system effectiveness, adjoining-structure settlement, sub-horizontal drain effectiveness
sections.applicability: Construction-phase supervision checklist covering general geotechnical items and, specifically, ground-water control and dewatering.

sections.title: Annex J.3: Performance monitoring
sections.summary: Post-construction/in-service monitoring items: periodic settlement (incl. vibration effects on metastable soils); lateral displacement/distortion (fills, stockpiles, soil-supported structures, deep trenches); piezometric levels near deep drainage/dewatering or deep basements; retaining-structure deflection under backfill/stockpile/surcharge/water loads; drain flow measurements; special problems (high-temperature structures causing desiccation, low-temperature/cryogenic structures causing ground freezing and frost heave); water tightness; vibration measurements.
sections.body: Annex J.3 lists items for performance monitoring of the completed structure: (1) settlement at established time intervals of buildings and other structures, including settlement due to the effects of vibrations on metastable soils; (2) lateral displacement and distortions, especially those related to fills and stockpiles, soil-supported structures such as buildings or large tanks, and deep trenches; (3) piezometric levels under buildings or in adjoining areas, especially where deep drainage or permanent dewatering systems are installed, or deep basements are constructed; (4) deflection or displacement of retaining structures, considering normal backfill loadings, effects of stockpiles, fills or other surface loadings, and water pressures; (5) flow measurements from drains; (6) special problems, including high-temperature structures such as boilers or hot ducts (desiccation of clay/silt soils, monitoring of temperatures and movements) and low-temperature structures such as cryogenic installations or refrigerated areas (monitoring of temperature, ground freezing, frost heave, and effects of subsequent thawing); (7) water tightness; (8) vibration measurements.
key_points: Ongoing settlement monitoring at set intervals, including vibration-induced settlement on metastable soils
Lateral displacement/distortion monitoring for fills, stockpiles, soil-supported structures, deep trenches
Piezometric-level monitoring near deep drainage/dewatering systems or deep basements
Retaining-structure deflection monitoring under backfill/stockpile/surcharge/water loading
Drain flow measurements and water-tightness checks
Special thermal problems: desiccation under high-temperature structures; ground freezing/frost heave under cryogenic/refrigerated structures
Vibration measurements as part of ongoing performance monitoring
sections.applicability: In-service performance monitoring checklist for completed geotechnical structures and their surroundings.
